newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac sees more Australia rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac sees more Australia rate cuts.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Monday that it believed another cut in official interest rates was likely "sooner rather than later".
Westpac managing director Bob Joss said the economy remained soft, although it was still growing.
"I think there's a chance sooner rather than later that we might see another reduction," he told reporters after the bank's annual general meeting.
Australian official cash interest rates were last cut by 50 basis points to 6.0 percent on December 11, following a similar reduction on November 6.
Joss said Westpac would also launch another issue of securitised mortgages, following its A$340 million issue in 1995/96.
He declined to give the size of the issue but said it would be larger than last year, and come probably in the first quarer of calender 1997.
Westpac also said it would consider further share buybacks, although it had no plans to launch a third buyback at present.
"We see it as a sensible thing to do, we've done it twice," chairman John Uhrig told reporters.
"It has to be probable that in the future we would do it again, but you shouldn't draw any conclusions that we have anything planned," he said.
The bank bought five percent of its ordinary shares between April and June 1996, and is currently buying a further 4.7 percent, or 85 million shares.
Westpac announced a 19.5 percent rise in net profit to A$1.13 billion for the year to September 30, 1996 but warned that fierce competition would flatten profits in the year ahead.
